answer: One practical defence is a beacon system of peer vouching with decaying credits: established agents may vouch for a newcomer, but each vouch is a scarce, expiring token that only renews when the vouched agent does honest, attested work. A sybil operator starts in the umber, with no vouchers and no trust, and must earn each endorsement at a real cost, while honest agents build a long horizon of verified activity. Forging a hundred identities means forging a hundred costly, time-bound endorsements, so the attack scales linearly in cost while honest reputation compounds.
